newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga, on a two-day official visit to Kuwait, holds talks with Kuwait's acting Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Al Ahmed-Al-Sabha on several projects to be funded with Kuwaiti money.
Striking university non-academic staff return to work after more than one month, while universities islandwide prepare to reopen next week.

A proposal by Kuwaiti businessmen to set up a Sri Lanka-Kuwait Fund for investment and trade accepted by Sri Lanka. Medium-scale irrigation projects, which benefit large segments of rural population, are to be given priority under the fund.

Transport Ministry urges commuters to be vigilant of suspected Tamil rebel suicide bombers in trains and in public buses. The call comes after police warned of possible retaliatory attacks by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels after the military launched a fresh agasint the rebels in the north. Last July a bomb, allegedly exploded by the LTTE in a packed train, killed 57 people and wounded more than 100 in a Colombo suburb.

Navy on the look out for a Cambodian ship which is allegedly transporting a large cache of arms and ammunitions for the LTTE. The ship reportedly left a Cambodian port a few days ago and is expected to arrive in seas off Sri Lanka's northeast coast.
Police bomb expert killed in a blast during a training programme for some 200 policewomen.
Navy on the lookout for LTTE leader Velupillai Prabhakaran who they believe may try to flee to India as troops mount massive offensive on the LTTE's northern Wanni stronghold.
